shipReasons: No critical defect in the changed area: FFX chapter 1 was reached from the title screen with nothing but real Enter presses, the first-turn coach mark now appears over a live command menu, one Enter dismisses it without leaking into the menu, and a real command run through the menu advanced the engine (battleLog 3 -> 14).

No regression against live 8f48237: the live build was opened in the same session at 1600x900 and 390x844. Everything that works live still works here, and the three things this candidate changed all measure better here than live (OD label 11.0 -> 12.25 px effective, 'I hide' 11.5 -> >=12, phone pause tab 25 -> 44 px, selected tab off-screen 4 of 8 -> 0 of 8).

Both majors are disclosed, not holds. FOC-05 lives entirely inside the brand-new onboarding feature, which does not exist on the live site at all, and is dismissed by the one key its own prompt names. FOC-06 was measured identically on the live build in the same session, so it is inherited, not introduced.
The four issues the previous focused review left open (FOC-01 to FOC-04 on 5e92289) are all fixed and re-measured with real input here.
npx tsc --noEmit clean; 92 changed-area unit tests pass across the four test files this batch added or changed.

checks.state: battle, first turn, coach mark up

checks.reason: No developer vocabulary in the changed surfaces: the coach lines, the pause tab labels and the pause body copy read as player text ('He moves after you. Not before. Use it.', 'H HIDE PANELS', 'ESC RESUME').

The FFX coach mark's plate is drawn over the move advisor card rather than beside it: mark rect [448,99,400x145] against card rect [402,98,370x189], an overlap of 324x145 px, so the card's title, the pick and its cost chips are behind an opaque panel for the whole of the first turn. See FOC-05. Nothing covers a painted actor: the party, Seymour Flux and Mortiorchis are all clear of the HUD at 1600x900.

Every pause tab label renders in full at 390x844 and no name is truncated: member:tidus, member:yuna, member:kimahri, chapter, guide, options, controls, music all measured with their full text width (46.3 to 90.8 px) inside a strip that now scrolls.

What is selected is obvious and now always on screen: cycling all eight pause tabs with real E presses at 390x844, the selected tab's rect stayed inside [0, 390] on all eight (scrollLeft moved 0 -> 7 -> 104 -> 186 -> 273 -> 332 -> 324). It was 4 of 8 off-screen on the previous candidate.

Everything claimed here was driven by the player's own input. FFX chapter 1 was reached from the title with real Enter presses only (title -> chapter-select -> party-prep -> cutscene -> battle, no debug navigation); pause was opened and closed with real Escape, tabs cycled with real E, panels hidden and restored with real H. The debug API was used only to read state and, for the two non-entry captures, to set up the chapter.

Every capture asserted its screen and state first: waitForFunction on __pyreflyReady, then on screen() === 'battle', then on the command stack having children, before any screenshot. No capture was taken after a failed wait.

This is a pre-deploy focused review of the immutable production candidate, not a live review. The live site was opened only as the regression baseline for the ship tags. The candidate's own live obligation is created by the deploy.

The shared work landed in both games where it is shared. The pause tab scroll fix, the 44 px tap target and the capture-phase confirm swallow are all in shared files and were checked in FFX chapter 1 and FFX-2 chapter 4; both games reach a real command menu with the coach layer active.

Presence in the intended game and absence in the other were both checked. FOC-01 is FFX only and its commit says so: in FFX the html carries data-coach-mark-game='ffx', the menu is open (7 rows) and .mad__card is opacity 1; in FFX-2 chapter 4 the flag is 'ffx2', Rikku's line is up, the menu is open (3 rows) and .mad__card is deliberately opacity 0, so one-teaching-surface-at-a-time still holds for FFX-2 alone, which is what coach.css's new [data-coach-mark-game='ffx2'] selector is for. FOC-04 is FFX only (ffx-hud.css alone; the FFX-2 HUD was untouched). FOC-02 and FOC-03 are both, in shared pause CSS, and were measured in both games' pause screens.

No chapter was played to a win or a loss in this pass, so the outcome half of the check is unproved, exactly as the previous focused review recorded. Entry and pause/resume transitions were proved: title to battle on real keys, Escape into pause and back to battle four times across both games.

Both changed subsystems were invoked through the real presentation path, not a harness: PauseView.scrollActiveTabIntoView ran because a real E press re-rendered the strip (scrollLeft moved), and CoachLayer/CoachMark ran because the real first FFX turn raised the mark from a cold context.
